solution: Let \(a=\sin^{-1}\frac{4}{5}\), \(b=\sin^{-1}\frac{5}{13}\), so \(\cos a=\frac{3}{5}\), \(\cos b=\frac{12}{13}\). Then \(\sin(a+b)=\frac{4}{5}\cdot\frac{12}{13}+\frac{3}{5}\cdot\frac{5}{13}=\frac{63}{65}\) and \(\cos(a+b)=\frac{3}{5}\cdot\frac{12}{13}-\frac{4}{5}\cdot\frac{5}{13}=\frac{16}{65}\), so \(a+b=\cos^{-1}\frac{16}{65}\). Hence \(a+b+\sin^{-1}\frac{16}{65}=\cos^{-1}\frac{16}{65}+\sin^{-1}\frac{16}{65}=\frac{\pi}{2}\), and the expression is \(2\pi-\frac{\pi}{2}=\frac{3\pi}{2}\). Matches option D.
note: partial sum written sin^-1(56/65); it is 63/65 (cos = 16/65), and the step to pi/2 is now shown. Key D unchanged.

solution: In \(\triangle ABD\), \(\frac{BD}{\sin\angle BAD}=\frac{AD}{\sin B}\); in \(\triangle ACD\), \(\frac{CD}{\sin\angle CAD}=\frac{AD}{\sin C}\). Dividing, \(\frac{\sin\angle BAD}{\sin\angle CAD}=\frac{BD}{CD}\cdot\frac{\sin B}{\sin C}=\frac{1}{3}\cdot\frac{\sqrt{3}/2}{1/\sqrt{2}}=\frac{1}{3}\cdot\sqrt{\frac{3}{2}}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}\). Matches option C: \(\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}\).
note: the ratio used sin C / sin B (that gives sqrt6/9, not the stated 1/sqrt6); it is sin B / sin C. Key C unchanged.

solution: Factoring: \((3\sin x - 1)(\sin x - 2) = 0\), and \(\sin x = 2\) is impossible, so \(\sin x = \frac{1}{3}\). Since \(\frac{1}{3} > 0\), there are two solutions in each interval where \(\sin x > 0\): \((0,\pi)\), \((2\pi,3\pi)\) and \((4\pi,5\pi)\), and none where \(\sin x < 0\). Total 6 solutions. Matches option C: 6.
note: said each period gives 2 roots except a 'last partial period'; roots lie only where sin x > 0, two in each of (0, pi), (2pi, 3pi), (4pi, 5pi). Key C unchanged.
